verdict: Section 6.8 is in good shape: Figures 17 to 40 are numbered consecutively and uniquely across the whole report with captions matching the text, Table 14 is referenced once in the text and its rows match the subsection correspondences, and every Sepolia fact (contract 0x0EC3...ADc73, chainId 11155111, solc 0.8.34, tokens #1 and #2, blocks 11,771,243 / 11,771,307 / 11,771,581, the three transaction hashes, selector 0x1e1e7c76 = mintConsentV3, 60 ledger events with 9 access requests and 5 anchors, 23 automated tests, signer prefixes 0x3Af549b0 and 0x39B12b87) was verified against the repository evidence files and is identical in Chapters 7 and 9 and Appendix A; no Claude or GitHub mention appears anywhere in the built report. The single citation [20] is correctly used, the component E naming (authorisation evidence) and the six lifecycle states match Sections 6.1 and 6.5, and the four blue additions read acceptably (one awkward 'in the same way'). The items that matter are the misleading statement that the plaintext purpose never leaves the application (it is in the public mint calldata), the sentence claiming screenshots follow Table 14, and the Chapter 7 claim that temporal expiration and policy violation were demonstrated live, which contradicts 6.8.6; with these fixed the section is ready for submission.
